correctness.rationale: For each skew tent map, full-affine-branch arguments give the complete first-order sign Markov law and stationary weights. The product chain restricted to equal-sign pair states gives exactly Q=[[0,1],[(1-c)(1-d),cd]]. Cayley–Hamilton gives the F_n recurrence; direct F_1,F_2 imply positive H_1 and the Cassini identity H_(n+1)=-(1-c)(1-d)H_n for all n, yielding strict alternating nonzero Hankel determinants. An order-m Markov process would have eventually constant conditional continuation of an all-zero history, a contradiction. Positive hidden transitions produce full binary support; primitive product transitions yield exponential mixing. The independent original-map rational interval checker passed 84 exact checks, but finite checks are not used as infinite proofs.
